Messages.Author: Creature
Messages.Body:
I remember a discussion a while back on what formula WW use to
calculate a vampire's capacity. Something along the line of 1 CAP for
every inf. discipline, 2 CAP for every SUP discipline, 1 CAP for every
vote, and then a modifier based on special ability. This formula works
pretty well when going thru the list of current vamps.

But when compared to what we've seen of the CE (Esau, Vitel), well, I
tend to see that CE vamps might be a bit on the powerful side when
compared to their predecessors. There are no current vamps with 10 CAP
that have 5 SUP disciplines (except Huitzichose). We've already seen 2
from the CE.

Is this the inevitable "dial-a-vamp" happening? Might this be a
"marketing strategy" to sell a set that has nothing to offer but 15
new minion cards and a bunch of re-writes that seem to piss off most
players???

If what we've seen continues, although I don't want to acquire this
set, I just might have to...

Thoughts?

Sir Ralph Hamilton:
6 points of disciplines. Cornercase advantage and disadvantage either even each
other out or each count as 0. 6 points is right on track.

Esau:
10 points of disciplines. +1 bleed is worth a point and we'll let his toin coss
bleed be worth another point. Note of course that his is worse than the IC
member's permanent +2 bleed since Esau has to burn a blood and only has a 50-50
chance of getting that last +. Of course I still find yet another vampire that
can naturally bleed for 3 to be a bit uncomfortable but I suppose it could be
worse. 12 points is right for a 10-cap.

Marcus Vitel:
10 points of disciplines
1 point for Princedom
And then ick.

You could argue that his retainer burn ability is a bit corner-case, but it
really depends on how common you see retainers in your meta-game. I'd give it a
full-point but I'll compromise and let it count as 0.5.

The other special is insanely powerful IMO. Yes, Marcus needs to be ready and a
Prince (remaining a Prince shouldn't be *that* hard for him). But since it can
potentially give +1 bleed to every vampire you control, I think the special is
more than a bit overpowered. I can imagine a Lasombra weenie deck (hi there
Christian!). 6-7 Lasombra weenies and Embraces might not look too threatening
until Vitel comes out and all the weenies now have +1 bleed...

I still maintain his bleed special is potentially too powerful, but overall
Vitel does seem to come out about right cost-wise.

(Let's just hope that whoever posted the "spoiler" was wrong about the Tremere.
We wouldn't want our precious 10-caps shorted by a point now would we?)

Halcyan 2

Well, beyond this discussions about crypt there has been a few details that
shocked me. On one hand, we have a bunch of highpowered ten caps. We've met
two of them (Esau and Lucius, sorry, Marcus), Jaroslav Pascek, if it comes
as some people has assured, is an almighty combatant. Also, we know of
Menele and Helena from the RPG, and both are extremely powerful. If it goes
like this, it's obvious that WW wants to encourage the metagame to one on
one Titan struggle rather than a bunch of influenced minions.

This vamps and some of the cards. The new derange only affects younger
vampires. Baltimore's Purge text is so specific and new in concept to this
game as to believe this is not a bluff. BP also benefits the use of high cap
vamps, so you should remain safe from them.

So, we have high cap vamps and an environment for them. Why am I worried,
then? Well, maybe because I have always preferred two 6 caps than an Inner
Circle. Maybe because putting of this monsters in play is one-third your
starting pool. Having this in mind i agree with ww to depower fifth trad, as
that will give cam decks the same possibilities of bringing 2 of these guys
as sabbat decks, it's obvious. But it won't turn games to faster ones.
Instead, most of the decks will be plenty of heavy pool gaining, ancient
influence, honor the elders, political stranglehold, and so, along with
better defense to avoid your pokemon being killed.

Weenie decks wil remain as they are now. Sure, pre weenie and embrace weenie
will disappear, but the main target of this new cards and rewordings are
clan midcaps. Decks with a 4-7 cap crypt will loose more than they'll gain
with all this, even though they are the most "fair" decks someone could
play. They are not outstanding in disciplines spread other than their
in-clan, they usually have lesser specials (except !toreador,perhaps). Most
of them are lame on one(or more) of the aspects of game (brujah don't know
what intercept/deflect is, ventrue lack of combat offense and intercept, and
malks are really "soft" when you achieve to catch them) and the whole fail
when facing politics. I won't say it saddens me. Well, my palla grande deck
won't remain as mighty as it is right now. When I thought of a classical
style brujah deck the one that comes to my mind it's the brujah debate deck,
not the Allmighty Jaroslav one.

Decks build around clans are for extend the standard way. But with all this
10-caps around and new/rewritten cards decks will be "a ventrue deck" no
more, they will be a "Marcus-Arika-Leandro" deck or an "Esau deck" or
whatever.

This big ten-caps are similarly powerful to their sabbat/independent
counterparts (Jaroslav/Lazverinus, Esau/Huiztilopochtli) , and I'm not sure
being glad of having a titan able to play 5 disciplines wich I would usually
play 3 in a given deck, or play with him alone with a 150 cards library. I
don't think this is the way to speed up the game, either.

Tom,Mad&Co

Remember: This is V:TES, not V:TM. A minion's "power" is limited by
cards in hand. It doesn't matter what disciplines a vampire has, if
there are no cards in hand which take advantage of those disciplines.
Along the same lines, you're not going to use more than 7 or 8 cap
worth of points (including titles/specials) for any given vampire. So
any other disciplines a vampire has, above and beyond those, are
usually superfluous for any one deck. Hence, 'points' are an invalid
metric for measuring either ability or worth for any vamp 9 cap or
higher.

Also, I think newer large-cap vamps with more 'points' (even if
points were a valid metric), reflect inadequacies with the earlier
vamps, moreso than excess with the newer vamps.

<snip>

> I doubt that you will "have to"...I greatly suspect that a number of the old

Old number of vampires remaining competive? Compared to what?
Certainly not to the new vampires in the Camarilla "set."

The sects were balanced previously due to the Sabbat having better
crypt cards and the Camarilla having better library cards (parity
shifts, traditions, etc.) It seems that the new set is making the new
Camarilla vampires more powerful at the expense of decreasing the
power of the Camarilla cards (if the paying for 2nd and the
limitations of 5th are true.) Is that White-Wolf trying to 'tweak'
the game to make it more balanced or are these marketing decisions?

The jaded and disenchanted of us see it as entirely marketing. Why
would a player who played Jyhad buy this set at all? There are only
FIFTEEN new library cards and fourteen of these don't require a clan
or discipline to even play (according to the list in Game Trader.)
Equally, the new cards look entirely different and for those of use
that were hesitant to mix Jyhad and V:tes versions of the same card,
we're certainly not destroying our decks with these new versions of
old substitutes. There will be four versions of some cards when this
set comes out (ex: Cloak the Gathering: Jyhad/V:tes/new art reprint
in set/Camarilla.) I most definitely do not a card that does the
exact same thing to look four different ways when in my hand. Thus,
players of Jyhad are less likely to buy Camarilla for the library
cards.

Turning to the crypt cards: White Wolf clearly realized this
inadequacy and (again for the disenchanted) decided that they would
compensate this by making the new vampires vastly superior to the
original - thus attempting to entice the old market to purchase
Camarilla packs for the more efficient vampire. Supporters of White
Wolf will offer the excuse of the "revised point system" as the reason
that the original princes and justicars are vastly inferior to their
new counterparts? But why did the system get revised? Exactly -
marketability. More powerful vamps = more profits from the older
player demographic.

As for the original crypt being competive: examine the old crypt
selection verses the very limited one that we have seen from spoilers
and previews looking at 8+ capacity vamps:

Dr. Jest (6 disc. points, a vote, and discard) 8 capacity = 7.5 points
with little compatability as he only has one in-clan superior.

Sylvester Simms (7 disc, a vote, torpor loss) 8 cap = 8 points being
generous

Roxanne, Rectrix (9 disc, vote, rush) 9 cap = 10.5 with four
superiors, good weenie rush potential - thus far, the only one I'd
call competitive.

Lucian (8 disc, 3 vote, equip steal) 10 cap = 10 points

Now Esau -the-Baali-in-Training:
Esau (10 disc, +1 bleed, chance for +1 bleed) = 10 cap for 12 points,
being 4 superior stealth bleed disciplines with bleed bonus specials.
The capacity to point ratio is clearly unbalanced when compared to
Lucian and if you factor in that tradition cards are less potent now,
then Lucian is of even less value!

Now the Ventrue compared to Vitel:

Emerson Bridges (7 disc, 2 votes) 8=8

Natasha Volfchek (7 disc, vote, +1 bleed, +vote stealth) 9=9.5 though
she doesn't have superior dominate.

Helena Casimer (8 disc, vote, +1 bleed) 9=9.5 though again not all 3
in clans at superior.

Democritus (7 disc, 3 votes, +1 bleed, contest cost) 10=10 without
all 3 in-clan superiors.

Compared to Vitel:
Marcus Vitel (10 disc, 2 votes, retainer burn, +1 bleed Sabbats)
Sabbat 10=13 *with* all 3 clan superiors and second ability which I
will save my ranting energy for another time, though likely to raise
more diatribe from me than Esau to my poor Jyhad list-serve.

Now we all know the Prince of D.C. is getting stronger (winning
qualifiers here and there and a regular bane to be at the mercy of his
infernal table negotiations ;-) but Emerson compared to Vitel seems to
take the Duffin success a bit far! (albeit Kudos on the
accomplishments Josh, the few evil bones I have in my body for Jyhad,
I attribute in part to you and Colin Riggs. =) )

But back to the ranting... Justification for the disparities in
vampires? "New point system," which now must be code for White Wolf's
marketing department. What will they do when they want to release
more Camarilla vampires - 10 capacity vamps with 15 points?

My long-awaited point is that the original vampires are simply not
competive at all compared to the very few that have been publicly
circulated from the Camarilla 'set' and balance of game play is not
the reason for this lacking - profits are. It seems to me (again in
the growing disenchanted group of former loyal players) that CCG
companies that make their decisions concentraing on profits over
playability, that the new players have little incentive to buy the
product. Why not simply buy the new Uber vamps from individual card
distributors or e-bay; old players who have played and supported this
game a long time voicing their complaints with their pocket books?
Again, I truly don't need a *forth* version of Cloak the Gathering.

Brad
finding it vastly appropriate that a Malkavian has replaced Cardano in
Boston and an evil, machiavellian type has replaced Emerson Bridges in
D.C. The irony.

The below is reprinted from
http://groups.google.com/groups?q=point+system+group:rec.games.trading-cards
.jyhad&start=20&hl=en&lr=&ie=UTF-8&selm=8rje8v%249vn%241%40nnrp1.deja.com&rn
um=21

The System (Peter Bajika)

I don't think anyone is completely sure that there ever was an actual
formula used to make the Jyhad set vampires, but as all of them were
pretty balanced in terms of abilities vs. capacity, we all came up with
one to use as a judge for the cost effectiveness of vampires. The
original vampires tended to fit in the following system:

Vampires of size 2-4: They got one less point in
disciplines/abilities than their age--i.e. a 2 point vampire got one
point of skills, a 3 point vampire got 2 points of skills, a 4 point
vampire got 3 points of skills.

Vampires of size 5-8: They got points disciplines/abilities equal to
their age--i.e. a 6 point vampire got 6 points worth of disciplines and
special abilities.

Vampires of size 9-10: They got one or two points of extra abilities
over and above the amount equal to their age--i.e. a 10 point vampire
usuaully had 11 or 12 points of skills and special abilities.

Caitiff tended to have one discipline and a disadvantage, 2
disciplines and a severe disadvantage, or no disciplines and an
advantage (Smudge will be ignored no longer!).

Costs:

A basic discipline cost 1 point.
A superior discipline cost 2 points.
+1 bleed or +1 hand damage cost 2 points.
A title costs 1 point (many folks adhere to the cost scheme of
Primogen=.5 points, Prince=1 point, Justicar=1.5 points, with rounding,
but the end result is the same).
Most other special abilites cost 1 point.
Some special abilities end up costing 2 points to make the formula
work.
Most clan specific special abilities (like Rake's) are free.

For example:

Emerson Bridges (8): He has 3 superior disciplines (6 points), one
inferior discipline (1 point), and is a Prince (1 point).
6+1+1=8...Emerson's capacity.
Agrippina (4): She has one superior discipline (2 points) and one
inferior (1 point). 2+1=3...one less than Agrippina's capacity (because
she is 4 or younger).

Badger (6): 2 superiors (4 points) and 2 inferiors (2 points). 4+2=6.
Sebastian Marley (7): 1 superior (2 points), 3 inferiors (3 points),
+1 hand damage (2 points). 2+3+2=7.

Don Cruez (10): 3 superiors (6 points), 3 inferiors (3 points),
Justicar (1 point), special ability (1 point). 6+3+1+1=11...one more
than Don's capacity.

Anvil (6): 2 superiors (4 points), 3 inferiors (3 points), Primogen
(1 point). 4+3+1=8 points! Anvil is the original "broken" vampire--far
more effective for his cost than he should to be.

Now, this formula was well adhered to in the original set--most
vampires fit very well, assuming you are willing to accept that some of
the weird special abilities of the huge vampires are worth 2 points to
make everything fit well.
The expansion vampires (DS and AH) tended to follow this formula as
well, but the designers seemed more willing to ignore the formula when
they felt like it.
For instance, Judah (6) only has 4 points of skills and is a Primogen,
making him a point overcosted--he should be a 5 or have one more point
of abilities (like inferior obf).

With the Sabbat, the designers decided that most special skills were
only worth 1 point (even +1 hand damage and +1 bleed, which were worth
2 points in Jyhad, resulting in fairly weak vampires like Zack North,
Sebastian Marley, and Adrianne), and out of clan disciplines only cost
half. This design decision resulted in the Sabbat vampires being wildly
overpowered when compared to their Jyhad counterparts. Compare Sheila
Mezarin (6) to Adrianne (6). Sheila has 2 in clan superiors, one in
clan inferior, one out of clan inferior, and +1 bleed. Adrianne (6) has
3 in clan inferiors, one out of clan inferior, and +1 bleed.
According to the original design system, Sheila has 2 points more in
abilities than she should--the result being that Adrianne is completely
eclipsed by Sheila.

The System for the Sabbat Expansion (Carl Pilhatsch)

Ok, in Sabbat it was like follows:

1 point for being a non-Pander
1 point for each normal in-clan discipline
0.5 point for each normal out-of-clan discipline
add. 1 point for each superior in-clan discipline,
but every 2nd is free!
add 0.5 point for each superior out-of-clan discipline
1 point for each vote (bishop 1, archbishop 2, cardinal+priscus 3)
1 point for +1 bleed, +1 intercept, +1 hand damage, +1 stealth, each
appropriate cost for each special ability, mostly 1 point

In Sabbat, all vamps applied strictly to this formula.

For VTES, DS and AH, I don't know for sure, but you can apply the
formula and it works well (I don't know if there are any exceptions).

Agrippina is ok: 1 for being a non-caitiff, 2 for sup OBF, 1 for
inf pot (1+2+1=4).

Anvil: 1 non-caitiff, 3 for standard disciplines norm, 2 in-clan sup
(1 point, every second free!), 2 out-of-clan normal (1 point) and 1 vote
(1 point). (1+3+1+1+1=7) Still overpowered a bit.

The new system seems to be a hybrid of the two old systems. Disciplines and
Titles are costed like Jyhad but specials are costed like Sabbat.

Comments Welcome,
Norman S. Brown, Jr.
XZealot
Archon of the Swamp

once? Moody as a damn girl."

"Brad Kellogg" <odd...@gwu.edu> wrote

>
> Now Esau -the-Baali-in-Training:
> Esau (10 disc, +1 bleed, chance for +1 bleed) = 10 cap for 12 points,

Lucian was never of much value anyway though. Esau is what Lucian *should*
have looked like 7 years ago.

I disagree with your point count... 1 point for +1 bleed is right on target
but paying 1 blood for the *chance* to get another +1 bleed doesn't sound
that great to me.

Blood is a scarce commodity these days and I think most of the time I'd
rather keep my vampires with some blood on them. I suspect we'll see the
'anemia'-factor become a major problem (or strategy) in the near future.
With cards like Free States Rant and The Final Nights, as well as the
[rumoured] changes to cards like Majesty and 2nd Tradition, I think we'll be
seeing more Hunting Grounds, Jake Washington, etc hit the table. Without
fuel, what will make our vampires go? :)

Additonally, while I like Esau's disciplines, they're not all that
compatible when combined. Presence, Dementation and Dominate are all fairly
similar for bleeding purposes. Sure he can Social Charm + Seduction + Eyes
of Chaos but is he that much further ahead than he'd be by playing Govern
the Unaligned + Seduction + Threats? The combo of Presence and Dementation
has potential with three other vampires (so far) having this combination.
Not sure what to do with it yet but I like having the option available.

Cheers,

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
In message <c25aa70a.02071...@posting.google.com>,
odd...@gwu.edu (Brad Kellogg) mumbled something about:

>Camarilla packs for the more efficient vampire. Supporters of White
>Wolf will offer the excuse of the "revised point system" as the reason
>that the original princes and justicars are vastly inferior to their
>new counterparts? But why did the system get revised? Exactly -
>marketability. More powerful vamps = more profits from the older
>player demographic.

No. Supporters of White Wolf will point out that the old high-cap
vampires just plain sucked, to the point where if you weren't using
their EXACT discipline combination, it just wasn't worth ever putting
them in your deck.

This is because of the "weenie problem", something that has been stated
here several times. 9-caps or above take three turns to influence out.
In that time, you can get slaughtered by weenies, so the vampire who
hits the table on turn 4 had damn well better be able to take EXCELLENT
actions. Most of the original Jyhad high-caps weren't designed with
this in mind; they just didn't realize that two 4-caps are worth more
than one 8-cap, because of the action advantage.

There's also the eggs-in-one-basket disadvantage; if I Pentex your big
guy, you're fucked until someone decides to help you... It's a lot
easier to put one vampire in torpor than 4... And any of a number of
other reason why big vamps are very risky to play with. To offset that
risk, big vamps HAVE to kick ass. This is something the original
designers simply didn't realize.

>As for the original crypt being competive: examine the old crypt
>selection verses the very limited one that we have seen from spoilers
>and previews looking at 8+ capacity vamps:
>
>Dr. Jest (6 disc. points, a vote, and discard) 8 capacity = 7.5 points
>with little compatability as he only has one in-clan superior.

Worthless vamp except in extreme corner-case.

>Sylvester Simms (7 disc, a vote, torpor loss) 8 cap = 8 points being
>generous

Worthless vamp except in extreme corner-case.

>Roxanne, Rectrix (9 disc, vote, rush) 9 cap = 10.5 with four
>superiors, good weenie rush potential - thus far, the only one I'd
>call competitive.

Disciplines that aren't worthless, but they can all be found on cheaper
vamps except for OBF/FOR... not a particularly winning discipline combo
(witness the Samedi).

>Lucian (8 disc, 3 vote, equip steal) 10 cap = 10 points

Comes with three in-clan superiors, a functional special, and is STILL a
Justicar, something which cannot ever be discounted. It's not just the
Traditions... it's cards like Parity Shift and the like as well.

And you can't imagine how useful 3 votes at a table can be, even if
you're not actively using them yourself.

>Now Esau -the-Baali-in-Training:
>Esau (10 disc, +1 bleed, chance for +1 bleed) = 10 cap for 12 points,
>being 4 superior stealth bleed disciplines with bleed bonus specials.
>The capacity to point ratio is clearly unbalanced when compared to
>Lucian and if you factor in that tradition cards are less potent now,
>then Lucian is of even less value!

No. Esau is plain and simply a stealth-bleeder, and that's all. He's
one hell of a bleeder, but I can get a bleeder who's almost as good for
half the cost. Going down his disciplines:

OBF/DOM/DEM/AUS -- Standard Malk/!Malk disciplines. Can be found
anywhere else. Dementation doesn't really add much to a stock
Malkavian, and Dominate only adds Deflection and Obedience to
!Malkavians. Sure, that's nice, but they already had Telepathic
Misdirection.

PRE -- Varies a bit, but OBF/PRE is easy to find, DOM/PRE is easy to
find, and AUS/PRE is easy to find. DEM/PRE is neat, so he almost fits
in a !Malk vote deck... except that he has no title, and can't be a
Cardinal, so why would you ever stick him in?

He looks awful good at first, but he's still a 10-cap, with all the
disadvantages listed above... not the least of which being that pesky
card Deflection. I'll pick plenty of other vamps to bleed with before I
go with Esau. And frankly, even though the Traditions may be less
potent, Esau still can't play ANY of them.

>But back to the ranting... Justification for the disparities in
>vampires? "New point system," which now must be code for White Wolf's
>marketing department. What will they do when they want to release
>more Camarilla vampires - 10 capacity vamps with 15 points?

Blithering and foolish paranoia.

>My long-awaited point is that the original vampires are simply not
>competive at all compared to the very few that have been publicly
>circulated from the Camarilla 'set' and balance of game play is not

Plenty of original vampires are MORE than competitive compared to these
two. Lucian and Esau are virtually equivalent; the Justicar title
easily makes up for the discipline shortage.

Vitel is noticeably better. Vitel is a promo card, and a 10-cap
himself. He still shares all the difficulties of other 10-caps, not to
mention a highly conditional special. Is he good? Yes. Is he
out-of-hand good? No.



> The sects were balanced previously due to the Sabbat having better

> power of the Camarilla cards (if the paying for 2nd and the

> the game to make it more balanced or are these marketing decisions?

Some of both, of course. I'd think the reason there are new
vamps at all is largely for marketing: they want to make new
cards because CCGs live through printing new cards, and they
don't want to make lots of new library cards because this is
a base set and the cards that should go in it already exist.
So, a bunch of new vampires. And if they really are doing the
"tweaking high-power cards" thing, obviously that's for balance
reasons.

I'd think it would be easier to "balance sects" using the same
approach rather than different approaches. Probably more "fair"
too.
